title: Data Residency (Customer One‑Pager) — Regions, Deployment Modes, and Telemetry
author: Olga Petrov
body:
## Purpose (approved for external sharing)
This one‑pager summarizes Redwood Inference’s **data residency posture**: (1) where Redwood can process and store customer content, (2) what controls are available by deployment mode (**Hosted**, **Dedicated**, **Private**), and (3) how **logs/telemetry** are handled.

**Scope note:** This page addresses *residency* (where data is processed/stored). For *retention* (how long data is kept), see: **Data Retention Controls — One‑Pager**.

---

## Definitions
**Customer Content**
- API inputs and outputs (e.g., prompts, chat messages, completions)
- Uploaded documents/attachments where applicable (feature-dependent)
- Derived artifacts such as embeddings generated from Customer Content

**Service Data (Operational Telemetry)**
- System and application logs (e.g., request metadata, error logs)
- Metrics and traces used for reliability, debugging, billing, and security monitoring

**Data residency** in this context means:
- The **primary region** where Redwood processes Customer Content and stores any configured persistent artifacts.
- Some **Service Data** may be centralized depending on the control plane, monitoring, and support workflows (details below).

---

## Region availability (Hosted & Dedicated)
Redwood offers customer-selectable regions for Hosted and Dedicated deployments. Availability can vary by model, capacity, and customer tier.

**Currently supported primary regions (typical):**
- **United States:** US region(s)
- **European Union:** EU region(s)

If you have a strict residency requirement (e.g., specific EU member state, UK-only, Canada, APAC), Redwood can review options for **Dedicated** and **Private**.

**How region selection works**
- You choose a **primary region** for your project/organization (Hosted) or cluster (Dedicated).
- Requests are **routed to that region** under normal operating conditions.
- Cross-region processing for Customer Content is **not part of normal operation** when a primary region is selected.
- Any cross-region failover behavior is **contract- and configuration-dependent** (see “Failover & resilience” below).

---

## Residency controls by deployment mode
### Summary table
| Topic | Hosted API | Dedicated (reserved capacity) | Private (VPC / on‑prem) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Where Customer Content is processed | In Redwood-managed cloud region selected by customer | In Redwood-managed cloud region selected by customer, on dedicated GPU pools | In customer-controlled environment (customer VPC or on‑prem), per deployment architecture |
| Where persistent artifacts may live (if enabled) | In-region storage by default for configured artifacts | In-region storage by default for configured artifacts | Customer-controlled storage and services |
| Customer control over networking | Limited (public endpoints + auth controls) | More control (dedicated endpoints, tighter isolation options) | High (private networking, customer routing, egress controls) |
| Telemetry / logs | Redwood-managed; some Service Data may be centralized | Redwood-managed; options may be available depending on contract | Customer controls most telemetry; Redwood access is scoped and depends on support arrangement |

### Hosted API (Redwood-managed)
**Best for:** fastest time-to-value with region selection.

Residency characteristics:
- Customer Content is processed in the **selected primary region**.
- Redwood operates the infrastructure, runtime, and control plane.
- Some operational tooling (e.g., monitoring, security analytics, support systems) may store **Service Data** outside the primary region depending on the subsystem.

Typical Service Data elements include:
- Request identifiers, timestamps, model identifiers, token counts, latency, error codes
- Security events (e.g., authentication events, administrative actions)

Redwood’s goal is to minimize the collection of Customer Content in logs; where content logging is necessary for troubleshooting, it is handled under controlled procedures and access controls.

### Dedicated (Reserved capacity)
**Best for:** predictable throughput and stronger isolation needs.

Residency characteristics:
- Customer Content is processed in the **selected primary region** on **dedicated capacity**.
- Dedicated deployments reduce multi-tenant operational coupling and can simplify certain residency and isolation narratives.
- Service Data handling is similar to Hosted unless otherwise specified; however, Dedicated may support additional configuration and support processes depending on contract.

### Private (VPC / on‑prem)
**Best for:** regulated workloads, custom network controls, and strict residency requirements.

Residency characteristics:
- Customer Content is processed within the **customer-controlled environment**.
- Data flows and residency are primarily determined by the **deployment architecture** and customer-selected infrastructure (cloud region(s) / on‑prem site(s)).
- The **shared responsibility boundary** changes materially: the customer controls network, compute placement, storage, and many logging/monitoring pipelines.
- Redwood may provide a private control plane and/or scoped operational access depending on the support model.

---

## Logs, telemetry, and auditability
### What Redwood typically logs (high level)
Redwood collects Service Data to operate and secure the service. Examples:
- Authentication and admin activity (SSO events, API key creation/rotation, role changes)
- System events (deployments, component health, autoscaling actions)
- Request metadata (timestamp, model, tokens, latency, status/error)

### Customer Content in logs
- Redwood’s standard operating posture is to **avoid** storing Customer Content in general-purpose logs.
- In some cases, limited content may be captured to diagnose incidents or customer-reported issues; access is restricted and auditable.
- Customers with heightened requirements should request Redwood’s **content logging posture** for their deployment mode and contract.

### Audit logs (customer-visible)
- Redwood provides audit logging capabilities in the Console for relevant control-plane and administrative actions.
- Availability and export options can vary by deployment mode.
- For detailed scope and export patterns, see: **Audit Logging Overview — One‑Pager**.

---

## Data flow differences: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
### Hosted
- Redwood manages the full data path from edge → routing → inference runtime → response.
- Customer network controls are primarily via authentication, IP allowlisting (if enabled), and configuration.

### Dedicated
- Similar logical data path to Hosted, but inference capacity and certain infrastructure are dedicated to the customer.
- Dedicated can reduce concerns related to “noisy neighbor” and may support contract-specific operational processes.

### Private
- The inference runtime and (often) supporting services run inside customer infrastructure.
- Customers can enforce strict controls such as:
  - Private network connectivity and routing
  - Egress restrictions
  - Customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM, where applicable)
  - Customer-managed log sinks and SIEM

---

## Failover & resilience (residency considerations)
Redwood designs for reliability; however, the **residency implications of failover** depend on configuration and contract:
- Some deployments may prioritize staying within a region even during incidents.
- Other deployments may allow cross-region failover to preserve availability.

If you have strict “no cross-region processing” requirements, please raise this during security review so Redwood can confirm the appropriate configuration and contractual language.

---

## Subprocessors and third parties
- Redwood maintains a subprocessor list and provides it upon request (and as required under applicable agreements).
- Subprocessors used for infrastructure, monitoring, and support can affect where certain **Service Data** is processed.

---

## Common customer questions (short answers)
**Q: Can I ensure prompts and outputs stay in the EU?**
A: For Hosted/Dedicated, select an EU primary region. For strict requirements (including failover behavior and Service Data handling), Redwood will confirm the configuration and any contract terms. For strongest control, consider Private.

**Q: Does Redwood train models on my data?**
A: Redwood’s platform is designed for inference. Any use of Customer Content for model training would require explicit agreement; if this topic is raised in review, use the approved response from the **Enterprise Security FAQ v2**.

**Q: Can I get logs into my SIEM?**
A: Redwood supports audit logging and provides export options depending on deployment mode and contract. See **Audit Logging Overview — One‑Pager**.

---

## How to request a residency review
If you have residency constraints (e.g., “EU-only processing,” specific countries, or no cross-region failover), provide:
- Deployment mode (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
- Target region(s)
- Any regulatory constraints (e.g., GDPR, financial services, health data)
- Requirements for logs/telemetry residency

Your Redwood Solutions Engineer can route questions to Security & Compliance for confirmation.

---
